newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: PRESS DIGEST - South Africa - Nov 25.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - South Africa - Nov 25.

text.p: These are the leading stories in the South African press on Monday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- The state expenditure department has signalled it will take a hard line against provinces claiming they need more money in their budgets, saying they have not even been able to spend their normal allocations.

- State telecommunications utility Telkom has announced several investigations and disciplinary hearings into the conduct of some of its staff in what it calls a "crackdown on irregular activities within the company".

- The European Union has indicated the 15-nation trading bloc could compensate South Africa's neighbours who might be affected negatively by a proposed free trade area between the EU and South Africa.
- Johnnic's newly appointed chairman Cyril Ramaphosa said the next phase of the economic empowerment process should focus on direct control of the manufacturing sector by black companies.

- Just weeks after the announcement of the five billion rand merger between pharmaceutical groups Adcock Ingram Ltd and Premier Pharmaceutical (Prempharm), the Adcock executive team has been replaced and nearly all of the main executive positions are now occupied by Prempharm staff.
- Economists responded enthusiatically at the weekend to reports that the government intends cutting its expenditure by two percentage points in real terms in the next financial year.

- Leading South African companies are handicapped by their poor knowledge of French, the lingua franca of countries that account for about 40 percent of the continent's trade, according to a survey by French language tuition group Alliance Francaise.
- South African navy divers were on standby to help with mop-up operations after a hijacked Ethiopian Airlines flight ran out of fuel and crashed into the Indian Ocean off the Comoros coast.
- A snap survey by The Star shows that more than 25 percent of the population might not have been counted in the country's census over the past two months.

- A Johannesburg nurse who contracted Ebola haemorrhagic fever from a Gabonese patient has died in an isolation ward, nearly a month after she was infected. Up to 350 people who might have had contact with the patient and nurse were being monitored for signs of the disease.
